routes.name: Residence Permit Class B (B-1, Specific employment by specific employer)
Residence Permit Class B (B-3, Specific employment by specific employer, Short Term Residence Permit)

note: Tanzania, read on the Immigration Services Department's own site (immigration.go.tz, rendered in a browser since its pages are drawn by script): its Residence Permit Guidelines (dated 17 February 2026 in its e-library) and its Service Fees page, on 2026-10-30. Fees are set in US dollars, so the file's currency is USD. A foreigner staying over 90 days for work needs a residence permit; Class B is for expatriates working for a company or private institution, on 'specific employment by specific employer' with a Labour Commissioner's work permit and an employment contract (work for the sponsor). Application must be made before the employee enters Tanzania, while outside the country (abroad); where a work permit is needed, both are applied for at once through the Labour Department's system (kazi.go.tz). B-1 costs US$2,000 (US$500 for citizens of the East African Community, not held by the form), plus a US$50 re-entry pass per applicant and dependant, not kept. B-3, the short-term residence permit for specific employment of not more than six months, costs US$500 (US$250 for EAC citizens); its six months are a ceiling, not a fixed term, so no term is kept. The guidelines list 'Replacement' as the issuance status of one renewing after expiry, and Class B's requirements are set for that status too, so B-1 is kept as renewable. Neither page states a permit's term or a decision time, so none is kept. Class C-10, 'Professional Artist' (persons employed as a professional artist, on BASATA's or the ministry's approval and an employment contract), costs US$500 but the pages don't say what work it allows beyond that description, so it isn't written; Class A-1, the professional artist investor (shareholder and director of a BASATA-registered company), likewise. Permanent residence and naturalisation (the Tanzania Citizenship Act) aren't on these pages.

sources.title: Immigration Services Department, Residence Permit Guidelines
sources.said: All foreigners intending to reside in the United Republic of Tanzania for business, work, investment or any other acceptable purpose for a period of more than 90 days, are required to hold a residence permit from Tanzania Immigration Department. ... 2. Class B: For expatriates working in company/ private institutions. ... Application for residence permits should also be submitted while the applicant is outside the country. ... Replacement (RPL) - For applicant renewing his application after expiration. ... GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR RESIDENCE PERMIT CLASS “B” (FG, SG, RT, RG1, RG2 & RPL) ... Application must be made prior to the entry of the prospective employee into Tanzania. ... Work Permit issued by Labour Commissioner (Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar), ... Employment Contract,
